help.metaDescription: Learn how Cladle works: guessing the mystery animal, daily puzzles, free play, reading the tree, and what taxonomy and phylogeny mean here.
help.title: How to play
help.lead: Cladle is a guessing game built on real taxonomy. You try to name a hidden animal in as few tries as possible; after each guess, the game shows how your species fits next to the mystery animal on a branching tree.
help.roundP1: Use the search bar to pick a specie and submit it. A wrong guess still teaches you something as your animal is added to the tree beside the mystery animal. Shared branches show how “close” you are in an evolutionary sense, using ranks such as class, order, or family.
help.roundP2: You have up to {maxGuesses} guesses. Win by submitting the mystery animal before you use them all.
help.dailyP1: Each day, a new animal is selected for everyone to guess. The puzzle rolls over at 00:00 UTC. On your local clock, this happens at {localMidnightUtc}.
help.freePlayP1: Free play is for practice. Whenever you reset, you get a new random mystery animal with no waiting. Handy when you do not want to wait for the next daily puzzle.
help.treeP1: Tips (or leaves) of the tree are species you have guessed (and the mystery animal once you have found it). Intermediate nodes are clades. They are named groups that regroup the species you have guessed.
help.treeP2: Clades are calculated from the LCA (last common ancestor) between your guesses and the mystery animal, they mark a shared ancestor for the animals grouped there. They show which part of the tree your guesses have narrowed the answer to.
help.termsTaxonomyP: Taxonomy is the naming and ranking system for living things. This system include taxon of multiple levels, including kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. Cladle uses those ranks to compare your guesses with the mystery animal and to label clades.
help.termsPhylogenyP: Phylogeny is the evolutionary “family tree” of species, it describes who split from whom over time. The in-game tree is a simplified picture of relatedness. Nearby tips usually share a more recent common ancestry than distant ones.

privacy.metaDescription: How Cladle handles personal data, cookies, and player privacy under the GDPR and French law.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Cladle is designed to collect as little personal data as possible. This notice explains what happens when you use the site, in line with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and French data-protection law (Loi Informatique et Libertés).
privacy.controllerP1: The data controller (responsable du traitement) for Cladle is Baptiste Rousseau.
privacy.controllerP2: For any privacy request, use the contact button at the bottom of this page.
privacy.overviewP1: Cladle runs in your browser. There is no Cladle user account and no first-party analytics or advertising trackers. Game progress and preferences stay on your device unless you clear them. Hosting and third-party APIs may process technical connection data (such as IP address) as described below.
privacy.dataLocalStorage: localStorage: game state, puzzle history, and onboarding flags so progress survives refreshes and return visits.
privacy.dataIndexedDb: IndexedDB: a local cache of taxonomy and related API data to reduce repeat requests and improve responsiveness.
privacy.dataCookieLocale: remembers your language choice (English or French).
privacy.dataTechnicalP1: When your browser loads Cladle or calls third-party services, those providers may process technical data such as IP address, browser type, and request timestamps in their server logs. Cladle does not ask you for your name, email, or other identity information to play.
privacy.dataContactP1: If you email the controller, the content of your message and your email address are processed solely to respond to your request.
privacy.purposesP1: Processing is limited to operating the game and the website:
privacy.purposeGameplay: Providing gameplay and remembering progress/preferences on your device — necessary for the service you request (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)) and/or legitimate interest in a working, privacy-respecting game (Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacy.purposeHosting: Hosting and securing the website via Vercel — legitimate interest in making Cladle available and secure (Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacy.purposeApi: Fetching taxonomy data from iNaturalist so the game can work — necessary for the service (Art. 6(1)(b)) / legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacy.purposeContact: Answering privacy or other messages you send — legitimate interest or steps at your request (Art. 6(1)(f) / Art. 6(1)(b)).
privacy.cookiesP1: Cladle only sets the functional cookies listed above. They are used to store choices you make (language and reading font) and are treated as strictly necessary for a service you request. Under CNIL guidance, such cookies do not require prior consent.
privacy.cookiesP2: Cladle does not currently use audience-measurement, advertising, or social-tracking cookies. If that changes, this notice will be updated and, where required, consent will be collected before non-essential cookies are set.
privacy.recipientsHosting: Vercel Inc. hosts the site. Connection and delivery logs may be processed by Vercel as part of hosting. See Vercel’s own privacy documentation for details.
privacy.recipientsInat: iNaturalist (api.inaturalist.org / www.inaturalist.org) provides taxonomy search, taxon pages, and related media when Cladle or you request them.
privacy.recipientsNoSale: Cladle does not sell your personal data.
privacy.transfersP1: Vercel and iNaturalist may process data in the United States or other countries outside the European Economic Area. Where applicable, such transfers rely on appropriate safeguards provided by those organisations (for example Standard Contractual Clauses) under GDPR Chapter V. Opening iNaturalist links in your browser is subject to iNaturalist’s own policies.
privacy.retentionDevice: Device storage (localStorage, IndexedDB, preference cookies): kept until you clear site data in your browser, or until a cookie expires (readable-font is set for up to one year; the locale cookie follows the i18n module defaults).
privacy.retentionLogs: Hosting and API logs: retained according to each provider’s policies, typically for a limited operational period.
privacy.retentionContact: Email correspondence: kept only as long as needed to handle your request, then deleted or archived as required by law.
privacy.rightsP1: Under the GDPR and French law, you may have the right to:
privacy.rightObject: object to processing based on legitimate interests;
privacy.rightWithdraw: withdraw consent, where processing is based on consent (not used for Cladle’s current cookies).
privacy.rightsP2: Much of Cladle’s gameplay data lives only on your device: clearing site data in your browser is the most direct way to erase it. For other requests, contact the controller using the button below.
privacy.rightsCnil: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Commission Nationale de l’Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL):
privacy.analyticsP1: Cladle does not use first-party analytics, advertising networks, or similar trackers today. If analytics measurement is added later, this page will be updated before it is enabled.
privacy.minorsP1: Cladle is a general-audience educational game and does not knowingly collect personal data from children beyond what is described here. If you believe a child has provided personal data by email, contact the controller so it can be deleted.
privacy.changesP1: This notice may be updated when Cladle’s practices or legal requirements change. The “Last updated” date at the top will be revised accordingly.
privacy.contactP1: For privacy-related questions or to exercise your rights, use the contact button below.

winState.furthestEvolutionaryDistanceHelp: Distance from the mystery animal to the most distant animal shown in the tree. Higher means at least one far relationship appears in this tree.
winState.evolutionaryDistanceHelp: How close your best guess was on the taxonomy ladder: lower is closer to the mystery animal. When you did not find the mystery animal, this counts how many taxonomic ranks still separated your closest guess from the mystery animal's deepest level.
winState.learningFootnote: Every guess traces a real branch of life, take a moment to see how species connect.
